verses.text: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he ruled for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, but not with his whole heart.
As soon as the kingdom was firmly under his control, he killed the officials who had murdered his father the king.

But he did not kill their children. He obeyed what is written in the law, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Parents must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their parents. Each person must die for their own sin."

Amaziah gathered the people of Judah and organized them by families under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He counted the men twenty years old and older and found three hundred thousand chosen men ready for war, able to handle a spear and shield.
He also hired one hundred thousand brave soldiers from Israel for about three and a half tonnes of silver.
But a man of God came to him and said, "King, do not let the army of Israel go with you, because the LORD is not with Israel, with any of the people of Ephraim.
Even if you go and fight bravely, God will let the enemy defeat you. God has the power to help you or to make you fall."
Amaziah asked the man of God, "But what about all the silver I paid for the army of Israel?" The man of God answered, "The LORD can give you much more than that."
So Amaziah sent away the soldiers who had come to him from Ephraim and told them to go home. They were very angry with Judah and went home furious.
Then Amaziah became brave and led his army to the Valley of Salt. There he killed ten thousand men of Seir.
The army of Judah also captured ten thousand men alive. They took them to the top of a cliff and threw them off, and they were all smashed to pieces.
Meanwhile, the soldiers Amaziah had sent back and not allowed to fight attacked the towns of Judah, from Samaria to Beth Horon. They killed three thousand people and took a lot of loot.
After Amaziah came back from defeating the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir. He set them up as his own gods, bowed down to them, and burned incense to them.
So the LORD was angry with Amaziah. He sent a prophet to him, who said, "Why have you worshiped the gods of these people? They could not even save their own people from you!"

While the prophet was speaking, the king said to him, "Did we make you an adviser to the king? Stop! Why should you be killed?" So the prophet stopped, but said, "I know that God has decided to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my advice."
Then Amaziah king of Judah talked with his advisers. He sent a message to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come, let's meet face to face in battle."

Joash king of Israel sent back this answer to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thorn bush in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar tree in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' Then a wild animal in Lebanon came by and trampled the thorn bush.
You say you have defeated Edom, and now you are proud and boastful. Stay at home! Why ask for trouble that will make you fall, and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen. God made this happen so he could hand them over to their enemies, because they had worshiped the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel attacked. He and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other in battle at Beth Shemesh in Judah.
Israel defeated Judah, and every man of Judah ran home.

Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, at Beth Shemesh. He brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, about one hundred eighty meters.

He took all the gold and silver and all the objects found in God's temple, which Obed-Edom looked after. He also took the treasures of the king's palace and some hostages. Then he went back to Samaria.
Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived for fifteen years after Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, died.
Everything else Amaziah did, from beginning to end, is written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
From the time Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, people in Jerusalem plotted against him. He ran away to Lachish, but they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
They carried his body back on horses and buried him with his ancestors in the City of Judah.
